items.t: Chapter 11 (al-bāb al-ḥādī ʿashar): On the originations of the divine Mercy (al-ikhtirāʿāt al- raḥamūtiyya) and the radiant, shining lights, within the lights of Mercy [114]

To proceed: may God, exalted is He, sustain us and you with His felicity, and grant us and you success in the pure [object] of His will. For God, exalted is He, wrote a book in His pre-eternity with the hand of His ancient existence, seventy thousand years before He created the spirits — by the measure of those years whose day is the extent of fifty thousand years, multiplied by seventy thousand years, which is the secret of the signs of God, exalted is He, in His Book. In it He wrote what none other than He knows. Save that what has been conveyed to us is that which the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — alerted us to, by his saying, upon him be blessing and peace: ((God, exalted be His power, wrote a book before He created the heavens and the earth by seventy thousand years, and it is with Him upon His Throne; in it is: My mercy has outstripped My wrath.)) And this is a reality traversed therein, and drawn from it, by the possessors of understanding — those whom God has loved and whom God has guided to a straight path. In this reality they were drowned, and so were utterly engulfed in the oceans of bounties and of greatness. /fol. 64r./ They never weary of their gazing upon their Master, nor of their affirmation of oneness (tawḥīd), and so their thoughts spoke forth. They are the inheritors, of whom God, exalted is He, gave tidings in His saying, glorified and exalted: Those who inherit Paradise — they abide therein forever (Q 23:11); they are the ones made manifest by the realities of the lofty ranks throughout the perpetuity of the ages, and their witnessing of the absolute Abode of Mercy is according to the reality of what the sphere of delimitation is able to encompass of the composite letters. And in this is some indication for one whose understanding is refined and whose knowledge is subtle.

Know that when the Maker — exalted be His power — brought forth the highest pavilion (al-surādiq al-aʿlā), and seated it upon the Footstool of the most splendid rafraf, and clothed it with a robe of the lights of Splendour, and enthroned it, and crowned it with the crown of the highest Wisdom, and displayed it upon the realities of the pure elect in the degree of good pleasure — out of the absolute Day that is expressed as al-ʿamāʾ (the Cloud), which is pre-eternity — He then called out to the elect realities and the chosen bounties in His presence: "Pass forth from your essences, and from the thought of your retreats, and from the firmness of your feet upon the carpet of your expansion, and from the quarters of your meadows in the Presence of the highest Holiness, and from the perplexities of your isthmuses — the object sought, the spacious, the wide, which travels with you the paths of the sea of good pleasure. Deliverance: from beneath its feet, the celestial realms; and from its midst, the dominion-realms (malakūtiyyāt); and from your Footstools, its highest, the celestial finalities. So betroth her as a companion, and take her as a friendly path of wayfaring." And they answered His call: "O our Lord, we have no secret by which we might be guided to the secret of the secret, nor any subtlety by which we might witness the realities of the thought of thought, for it is, between us, an encompassing sphere and a simple figure." Then, when He knew from them this lowly tenderness and the original, derivative reality, God, exalted is He, opened for them that book whose mention has gone before and whose glory is renowned, and made them witness the Circle of the divine Mercy. Its secret was engraved upon their secret, and by its secret they looked out upon the innermost secrets of their secrets. And behold, it was a resplendent circle: it spread out as an ample mantle, and was ordered with an ample, noble ordering, which by its fragrant breath gave life to decayed dead bones. And behold, it is a circle having an exterior and an interior: its exterior is the secret of a circle established upon letters whose number is five hundred and sixty-seven, and its interior contains letters whose number is two hundred and thirty-one. So the ratio of the one hundred and thirty is a pre-eternal ratio, and it is the treasured one; and the ratio of the two hundred and thirty-one is a post-eternal ratio, and it is the Book written therein. Then, when there appeared to them from its utterance a knowledge that teaches, a secret that instructs, a divine effusion and a holy spirit, they did not cease to follow their traces, while it made clear to them the most exalted Truth. And so they found the power for concordance and for connection through the substance of concordance, and they took it as a leader for the Abode of Abiding and a provision for the Abode of Peace.

So when you desire that, verify the secret of the second number; then there will dawn upon you the first knowledge and the manifest, hastened secret. That is because the highest pavilion, over which the most exalted Footstool has ascendancy, is veiled by praise and by the most perfect splendour, through the secret of the intended within the intended; for it is a witnessed bringing-into-being within the units in respect of their ranks, not in respect of their enumeration. Understand that. For people, in this matter, stand upon three ranks of apprehension /fol. 64v./ and of the realities of unveiling. Whoever witnesses the first Book while it is still folded up witnesses the veils of the highest pavilion; whoever witnesses what is written in it witnesses the Footstool upon which the pavilion rests; and whoever witnesses the secret of the writing witnesses the uttermost pavilion, beyond which there is no further degree to ascend, save that which encompasses the secret of the All-Merciful Circle. And here I shall strike for you a likeness of this, one that brings it near to the understanding and makes it easy for knowledge. Posit a flat circle whose weight is balanced, and raise it up into the air without any support: its exterior is the above of the above, its interior the below of the below; its first is the first of the first, its last the last of the last; its right is its pre-eternity, its left its post-eternity. And of the circle which is the circle alif–jīm–dāl: its exterior is dāl–alif, and its interior is the interior of alif. So it is by the secret of the alif, not by the manifest alif, that there is a relation of the above of the above — since no "above" can be conceived. Its height is the alif traced at the top of the circle; its depth is by descent; its right is its jīm, and its left is its dāl. This — by the truth of the Truth — is the reality of divine oneness: without likening, without configuring, without comparison, without delimitation, without absoluteness; no above and no below, no right and no left, no behind and no before. Understand — may you be guided — for the time has drawn near for the appearance of the Reality and the witnessings of the Reality within the Way.

As for the secret of the raḥamūtī: it is the secret of the isthmus (barzakh) that lies between the two alifs which are shared in the interiors of the Circle and its exteriors. And you are the sum of the Circle, the witness of the Reality and the secret of the divine Mercy. So witness the pavilion, and give credence to the truthful, uncanny one (al-nukrī) [reading uncertain; ms. A: al-fikrī, "of thought"]. For if you unfasten the bezel of this signet ring, you will enter the garden of gnoses in peace. So branch out the branching of thought by the light of the divine Mercy: stand by it, and do not stand over it; for when you stand by it, you [truly] stand over it, and you establish toward it the essentiality of the secret, and the divine effusion of Mercy overflows. Then you will understand the limit of what came before by what came after, and what is hidden by what is manifest, so that the realities of things become bearers of good tidings for you — and if not, then warners against you, and you will be joined with those who lose most in their works, whose striving has gone astray in the life of this world while they reckon— in the world of the rafraf — that they are doing good work (Q 18:103–104) — in the world of the pavilion. The High, the Most High, has set them forth by His saying, exalted is He: Those are the ones who disbelieved— in the world of the veils — in the signs of their Lord— in the world of the Footstool — and in meeting Him — in the world of the pavilion — so their works came to nothing— on the Day of Regret — and We shall not assign to them— in the isthmus — any weight (Q 18:105) — on the Day of the Rising. That is their recompense: Hell— in the world of the veils — because they disbelieved— in the world of the Footstool — and took My signs— in the world of the highest rafraf — and My messengers— in the world of the uttermost pavilion — in mockery (Q 18:106). Had they entered the Circle of the divine Mercy, the dominion-secrets would have shown them mercy.

An admonition: that is [indicated] by His saying, glorified and exalted, There is no god but God— two circles, negation and affirmation. Is the circle of negation among the circles of affirmation, or among the circles of negation belonging to the one who professes [His] oneness, while the circle of affirmation belongs to the bringer-into-being? They are two halves: the half of negation, which lies in the things of knowledge, and the half of affirmation, which lies in the things of practice. /fol. 65r./ And since the half of negation comprises five letters, the things negated are five: the negation of the acts of choice among the volitions; the negation of your existence from the operative deployment of Power; the negation of your standing by works; the negation of your disposal by the Names; and the negation of your subsistence in the states. These five are among the attachments of the soul; and whoever severs these attachments is raised by it to the circle of affirmation — seven ranks, according to the number of its letters — so that his life may be by divine oneness, his knowledge by direct witnessing, his power by good pleasure, his disposal by wisdom, his gaze by insight, his witnessing by the Reality, and his hearing by unveiling. For by his life through divine oneness he grasps the reality of subsistence; by his knowledge through direct witnessing he beholds the lights of subsistence; by his power through good pleasure his soul is held back from [lacuna in the edition]; by his speech through wisdom he acquires his inspiration from the slip [reading uncertain; perhaps qaṣarat nafsahu ʿan al-zalal, "his soul is held back from error"]; by his gaze through insight he unveils the realities of the final outcome; and by his hearing — affirmation. For whoever has no negation has no affirmation. So whoever has had experience, and known, and been well pleased, and spoken with wisdom, and gazed with insight, and heard with the secret — that one is the one made excellent by the secret, and vision in the world of Reality becomes his due; and thereupon he reads the speech of God, exalted is He, according to the seven modes in which the Qurʾān was sent down. This, then, is the reality of gazing upon what has passed. And since There is no god but Godis twelve letters, and since these twelve letters are the fortress of God — as He, glorified and exalted, informed us by His saying, "There is no god but Godis My fortress" (the annexation to Him being thereby established) — and since the circle of the perfection of existent things among plants, minerals, and animals lies between the reality of the four seasons, and the four seasons contain twelve months, and the whole world is under the delimitation of the circle of the year: then the forms have been addressed in respect of their positing, and in respect of what has been apportioned to them in the first operative deployment along this Lordly path from which there is no turning aside, by the realities of the perfection of the determinations of measure — in its months, then in its days, then in its hours. Thus the twelve letters came to correspond to the twelve months, each month subsisting by a letter — rather, each letter emerging in a month. The months are the vessels of the letters: through them mercy descends, universality appears, wisdom gushes forth, guidance takes place, increase comes, benefits grow great, growth becomes great, fertility abounds, and good deeds multiply. This is in general terms. As for the detail: God, exalted is He, has made, out of His hidden gentleness and the subtlety of His wisdom, by what He deposited of the operative deployment of the year within the single day, a rank set over twelve hours, one hour facing each month, within which is the secret of that month. He placed the secrets of spring in the first three hours, the secret of summer in the second three hours, then the secret of autumn in the /fol. 65v./ third three hours, then the secret of winter in the fourth three hours. So every hour subsists by the secret of a letter among those temporal letters that build up divine oneness.

And since the day is twelve hours, and by it the [divine] governance is completed — for if the day of the servants were to continue unbroken, the very substance of the blessing would become a torment, since self-subsistence (qayyūmiyya) is not fitting

— save to al-Qayyūm (the Self-Subsisting). The human world is compounded of motion and rest, and there is no avoiding the divulging of them both and the unveiling of their phases. So God made the night, which is the being of its concealment and its return to the world of its reality, by the secret of transference and of resurrection, and the ascent of the spirits, and the rising up of the intellects, and the stillness of humanity beneath the pitch-black of darkness. So He made the night twelve hours, and the circle of "Muḥammad is the Messenger of God" was twelve letters, to each letter an hour. So then, as for "There is no god but God" — the affirmation of oneness is not completed by it save through "Muḥammad is the Messenger of God"; and likewise the circle of the day is not completed save by the circle of the night. Thus wisdom has been perfected in the night and the day by the intermingling of mercy, according to His saying, exalted is He: And of His mercy He has made for you the night and the day, that you may rest in it and that you may seek of His bounty, and that you may give thanks (Q 28:73). What is understood of that is that whoever says "There is no god but God, Muḥammad is the Messenger of God," under the condition of what we have mentioned and with the realization of that to which we have called attention, it is as though he worshipped God, exalted is He, with the worship of a full year. And therefore he — upon him be blessing and peace — said that the best remembrance of the prophets — upon them be blessing and peace — lies in his saying, God bless him and grant him peace: ((The best of what I and the prophets before me have said is: There is no god but God.))

Know that the twenty-four letters have set over against them twenty-four worlds: nine isthmus-realities (barzakhiyyāt), celestial and terrestrial; eleven spheres and circles — and to every world an innovation (ibdāʿ) — and four celestial ones, which are the realities of the first things of the world of origination (ikhtirāʿ). They are, then, twenty-four worlds; and in every world is the reality of a letter from among these luminous letters, so that by the letter's taking charge the manifestation of each one of these worlds is realized. And since the reality of this upper and lower world is a relation within the essence of the Throne, the secret of their fixity in it lay in the two lines written with the two lights — I mean the white light and the green light, and these two are "There is no god but God" and "Muḥammad is the Messenger of God." Those two luminous lines are beneath the Throne; and this is the reality of the spiritual subtlety. And since from the eight who bear the Throne — upon them be peace — there issue the spirits of the things of the Dominion (malakūt), the lights of the things of the Omnipotence (jabarūt), and the lights of the things of the sovereign rule (mulk), the whole world was lights, and the Light of lights, which is the Throne; and the Illuminator of the light is God, exalted is He, by His saying, exalted is He: God is the light of the heavens and the earth (Q 24:35). And to each angel belonged the light of three letters; there issues forth from the light of each letter that which befits the horizon of each malakūt, jabarūt, and mulk. /fol. 66r./ The light of the Dominion supplies the intellects, the light of the Omnipotence supplies the spirits, and the light of the sovereign rule supplies the heart; and so the twenty-four are completed for the eight angels, from the ratio of multiplying three by eight. Understand that. And therefore, whoever says "There is no god but God, Muḥammad is the Messenger of God" —

— he stirs toward the Throne's receiving [of it]. That is because the goodly word ascends by its own essence, since it has a relation in the sovereign rule (mulk), an ascension in the Omnipotence (jabarūt), and a rising in the Dominion (malakūt); so nothing of the realities of the worlds that issue from it attaches to it, nor follows after it below it. God, exalted is He, has said: To Him ascends the goodly word (Q 35:10). And therefore whoever says it a thousand times, in a state of purity, in the early morning of every day — God makes easy for him the means of provision in proportion to his relation [to it]. And likewise whoever says it when he goes to his sleep, with the number mentioned — his spirit passes the night beneath the Throne, feeding from that world according to its powers. And likewise whoever says it at the standing still of the sun — the satan of the inward is weakened by it. And likewise whoever says it at the sighting of the new moon — he is safe from sicknesses. And likewise whoever says it upon entering a city — he is safe from its trial. And likewise whoever says it with his thought gathered and sends it against an oppressor or a tyrant — he cuts him off. And likewise whoever says it with the intention of gazing into the celestial things — the unseen of what he intended is unveiled to him. All this is under the condition of what we have mentioned and the verification of what we have stipulated, namely the concurrence of the understanding of the secrets of the letters with the ordering of the worlds. For every world contains within it the names of the deeds and the intentions, according to his saying — upon him be blessing and peace: ((Deeds are only by intentions, and every man shall have only what he intended.))

And since the courts of judgement (ʿaraṣāt) are twelve, to each letter there belongs a station in which he who stands takes his stand within that court, and by that letter he ascends, and its manifestation shall be for him on the Day of the Greatest Gathering — that is, the Day of the Middle Mustering. This, then, is a subtlety that discloses the secret and opens the locks of thought. So the earth was changed into other than the earth; and that is because the sun-orb of the divine Mercy — which is expressed as the Light of lights and the pole of the abode — had revolved over the enigmatic essences, the obscure attributes, the premised distinctions, and the firmly established outward aspects; and it turned a turning of the heart, and a royal state took possession, just as length was exchanged for breadth, and the changing of the heavens and their folding was made binding — as the scroll is rolled up for the raḥīmī Book (the Book of the Compassionate), the dazzling light and the balance. Then, after that, the spirits were plunged into its surging sea, tumultuous with waves; and the spirits dived into those seas until there was reflected back, from the very source of darkness, a brand of fire for those who would warm themselves at it, and it blazes toward the magnified tree and the honoured issue, at the towering height of the Mount of speculation. And the outward [man] is not guided by its guidance, nor does he strive with its striving, save the evening-journeyer, the fragrance-diffuser, the wayfarer, the righteous; or the deep-diver, the lofty; or the absent one, the aspiring; and the faithful, the preponderant. /fol. 66v./ Or the faithful, the preponderant: for this is the shining forth of the tree of divergence and the dissolving away of the trace of disagreement. So understand this celestial subtlety, this dazzling wisdom-quality, and this Lordly bestowal. It lies within the secret of His saying, exalted is He: Say: I but exhort you to one thing — that you rise up for God, in twos and singly, then reflect: there is no madness in your companion (Q 34:46). And the exception made by thought is by the conjunction "then": "then reflect" — by the secret of unity (waḥdāniyya) and the secret of duality (mathnawiyya). For the secret of unity is the outpourer of the determinations of divinity, and the secret of duality is the outpourer of the human determinations. And it is not valid —

— the witnessing of unity is not valid save after the discernment of duality, and save by the reality of thought; and thought lies in the secret of the even, not in the secret of the odd, for the odd is pre-eternity and the even is post-eternity. So whoever witnesses by the secret of the odd within the secret of the even has come to stand upon the easing toward ease and upon the raising up within the stations made easy toward hardship.

Know that it is a day whose measure is fifty thousand years in the first rank, and a thousand years in the second rank; and it is likewise, in its measuring, in the third rank, as the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — measured it in his saying: ((like the two rakʿas of dawn)). So whoever has [the door] opened to him in the secret of unity, without the renewal of duality — for him the day is the fifty thousand years. And whoever partakes of duality with an admixture of unity — his day is like a thousand years. And whoever isolates thought from the two worlds — his day is like the two rakʿas of dawn; so he stands upon the heights of the deeds and recites over the tract of gladness and the letter of delight, which is:
Praise be to God, who has removed sorrow from us; truly our Lord is Forgiving, Appreciative (Q 35:34).

Know that the substance of the world, with its secrets terrestrial and celestial, its nearest and its furthest — nay, every mote that has been deposited within it — is only from the life deposited in the paradigm of water. In it is the secret of the making (jaʿl), and that is the first of the water; as for the last of the water, in it is the secret of life. Water is an isthmus (barzakh) between the two circles. So by the secret of the making the Dominion and the Omnipotence came to be, and everything outward rests upon the secret of life while in its inward is the secret of the making. The ḥāʾ of ḥayāt (life) is by the secret of ḥarāra (heat), and the jīm of jaʿl (making) is by the secret of jalāla (majesty): by it the secret of subjugation befell him, and by the ḥāʾ of life the secret of subsistence became his due. So the jīm of majesty was smelted between the sights of the hearts and the rivalry of the things of the Dominion; for by heat the bitterness of the light of life is drawn to the essence of the intellect, and so it split forth as a resplendent light. Thus from the necessity of existence there came heat and the jīm of majesty, since it is the secret of Lordship — for it belongs to the nature of Lordship [that there be] its divinity and intimacy. The Most High Truth has disclosed Himself through intimacy in the manifestation of the jīm and through the vision of the intermediaries; and the affirmation of oneness is the root in wisdom. In view of that is His saying, exalted is He: Say: Have you considered — if God should make the night unceasing over you until the Day of Resurrection (Q 28:71) — the verse. For were the jīm of the making to prevail with the darkness of contraction, operative deployment through wisdom would be lost; and likewise, were the ḥāʾ of life to prevail with the presence of expansion, the affirmation of oneness would be hidden away. Hence His saying, exalted is He: Say: Have you considered — if God should make the day unceasing over you until the Day of Resurrection /fol. 67r./ (Q 28:72) — the verse. Then God, exalted is He, made them a balance of justice and a sending down of mercy and bounty, for the manifestation of wisdom in the making-known and the manifestation of oneness in the bringing-into-being. And therefore God, exalted is He, said: And of His mercy He has made for you the night and the day, that you may rest in it and that you may seek of His bounty, and that you may give thanks (Q 28:73). This, then, is a perpetual (sarmadī) subtlety; it is the everlastingly perpetual.

Know that the pavilions (surādiqāt), the attachments, the lights that make manifest, veil over the lights of the intellect; and the raḥmānī pavilions are a manifestation within the secrets of the evenly-poised originated things; and the exalted pavilions are veiled by subtle thought. For the inward of the most radiant Dominion is from the light of the parts of the most splendid Dominion. So if you desire the understanding of that, then take to grasping this subtle indication: Take four of the birds (Q 2:260) — the hidden Name, the treasured Name, the veiled Name, and the Greatest Name — and draw them to yourself (Q 2:260); and make them familiar by the secret of intimacy, and pasture them in the Presence of Holiness. Then, when you have gained possession of the keys of their inmost reality and have witnessed the witnesses of their secret: Set upon every mountain a portion of them (Q 2:260) — upon the mountain of the pearl, the portion of the greatest bird; upon the mountain of the Omnipotence, the portion of the veiled bird; upon the mountain of the Dominion, the portion of the treasured bird; and upon the mountain of the uppermost rafraf (the celestial cushion), the portion of the hidden bird. Then call them (Q 2:260) by the secret of that which you commanded them, and they will come to you in haste (Q 2:260). And that is for one who has realized the name of might and the name of wisdom. So if you have understood this inspirational psychic [subtlety] and this luminous unveiling: Take four of the birds and draw them to yourself (Q 2:260) — the first is the bird of life, the second the bird of knowledge, the third the bird of power, and the fourth the bird of will. Realize life by the life of faith, through annihilation from sense-perception; and knowledge by the knowledge that brings one to God, exalted, mighty and majestic; and power by the secret of origination (ikhtirāʿ); and will by the secret of reflection upon innovation (ibdāʿ). Then place upon the mountain of the pearl by the secret of life; upon the mountain of reflection upon innovation, by the secret of knowledge; upon the mountain of composition, the secret of power; and upon the mountain of ordering, the secret of will. Then call them, and they will come to you in haste (Q 2:260). This becomes manifest to one who draws near to God, exalted is He, with his entirety, until he is qualified by His saying, exalted is He: "I am his hearing, his sight, and his tongue" — the noble hadith.

Know that the Fire complained to its Lord and said: O Lord, part of me has devoured part of me. So He gave it leave to breathe two breaths: one breath in winter and one breath in summer. These, then, are two differing breaths from a single essence; and the separating of the breath was made easy only through the presence of density — nay, through the hiddenness of the noble subtlety and the equity of the apportionment

— the High, and a bringing-into-existence by the faithful stipulation. So understand that from His words, exalted is He: And there is none of you but shall come to it (Q 19:71) — an expression for the day of this world. /fol. 67v./ As for the coming-to-it on the day of the hereafter, its station is its reality: Then call them and they will come to you in haste (Q 2:260). So if you have attained annihilation within subsistence, and witnessing within the encounter, then: So take four birds and draw them to yourself (Q 2:260) — the bird of prophethood, the bird of truthfulness (ṣiddīqiyya), the bird of martyrdom, and the bird of righteousness. Draw them to yourself and verify their existence within their witnessing. Then place upon each mountain a part of them (Q 2:260): upon the mountain of the intellect, the bird of prophethood; upon the mountain of the spirit, the bird of truthfulness; upon the mountain of the heart, the bird of martyrdom; and upon the mountain of the body, the bird of righteousness. Then call them and they will come to you in haste (Q 2:260). And if your standing in this station is made firm, you will witness within them these [modes of] understanding. So take four birds and draw them to yourself (Q 2:260): take the bird of the intellect, which is the secret of life; and the bird of life, which is the secret of knowledge; and the bird of the heart, which is the secret of volition; and the bird of the inmost secret, which is the secret of power. Then place upon each mountain a part of them (Q 2:260): set upon the mountain of the intellect the bird of the heart, and upon the mountain of barzakh-life the bird of the spirit, and upon the mountain of the life of the hereafter the bird of the inmost secret, and upon the mountain of everlasting life the bird of the heart. Then call them and they will come to you in haste (Q 2:260). And know that whoever clothes himself in the robe (ḥulla) of intimate friendship (khulla) — the witnessing of subjugation is not valid for him; for intimate friendship is the Lordly intellect, and the robe is the spiritual spirit, because Might has severed intimate friendship, and wisdom is the spirit of intimate friendship. If you desire [to know] how the connection is made with what we have intended and mentioned, then conform, in accordance with what we have made clear and set in order. So listen — may you be guided. One of the people of the realities — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with them — recounted, saying: I boarded a vessel the number of whose planks, gathered within it, was one hundred planks and thirty-one planks; and this is a condition in the ship of salvation. And I remained upon the sea, running with the wind of safety, in conformity [with that]. And the anchorage was five hundred and twelve — the span of the days of the four seasons — except that every day among the days of these four seasons is derived from that which is original within it. And I reached the shore of the sea, and I found precious jewels, and dazzling rubies, and mighty treasures, and red sulphur, and variegated mineral veins, and the spring of life flowing perpetually. So I washed myself in its water, and drank from it a draught after which there is no passing away. Then I drove my vessel [through] the days of God, and I returned toward my homeland; and my setting out had been from the rising-place of the sun to its setting-place — and there is the blessed shore. This, then, is a counsel manifest to the eye, apprehensible at every time and season. And God speaks the truth, and He guides upon the way. And we ask God, exalted is He, of His bounty; truly He is Knower of all things.

And know — may God grant me and you success — that the motions are four: a motion of unveiling, which is the first; a motion of veiling, which is the second; a motion of the unveiling of the unveiling, which is the third; and a motion of veiling, which is the fourth. The first motion of unveiling is the motion of the primordial atoms (dharr); it is the essential motion, and it is the motion of the intellect. And the first motion of veiling — it is the motion of the soul, /fol. 68r./ and it is a māʾiṣa motion [ ;reading uncertain — perhapsmāʾija, "surging"]. And the second motion of unveiling is the motion of the spiritual heart, and it is a volitional motion. And the second motion of veiling — it is the motion of the essences, and it is a motion of longing. And the motion of the first day is for the first day, which is the day on which God created the spirits in the world of the covenant. And the second day belongs to the first veiling: the addressing of the intellect in the world of motes — and these are the principles of the primal things. And the third day is the day of the second unveiling, which is the day of the taking of the covenant upon the primordial atoms. And the fourth day is the day of the second veiling, the day of the acceptance of consideration for the obligations imposed by the Law, and it is the day of the term (amad) — except that its end is the day of the first unveiling. So the first unveiling is the Throne of the First, and the first veiling is the Footstool of the First; then the second unveiling is the Throne of everlastingness; then the second veiling is the Footstool of the term. And all these phases and cycles are the reality of the All-Merciful nature (raḥmāniyya) and the right of the Compassionate nature (raḥīmiyya). For the reality of the raḥmāniyya is the secret of the admixture — the admixture of the subtle things (laṭāʾif) with the dense things (kathāʾif) — in known portions. And so the secret of Lordship comes forth within the secret of the admixture: I mean the inbreathing that is annexed to the Presence of manifest Lordship; and within its relation are the subtle things that are put to use by means of the dense things. This, then, is the secret of the veils — that is to say, this arising (nashʾa). The Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — drew attention to this in his words, reporting from his Lord, mighty and majestic: ((Truly God has seventy veils of light and of darkness; were He to remove them, the glories of [His] face would burn up whatever of His creation His sight reached.)) The second [point]: the veils are from your relation, not from His relation, for they are impossible from two aspects; and such [veils] veil nothing but a body, whereas the Real — glorified and exalted — is not a body. And know that the veiled must needs have a direction, whereas God — glorified and exalted — has no direction. So the veils of darkness are the veiling of the everlastingnesses from the primal lights, and the veils of light are the veiling of the primal things from the principles of the Essence. And the All-Merciful primal things — I mean their reality — are the relation of the dense things through the pervasion of the subtle things; and were it not for that, they would pass away. And know that the subtle things are the bearers of the dense things, and that the subtle things are such that their parts are then greater than the parts of the dense things. And here I am, drawing attention to it by a limpid subtlety and a surpassing fragrance, drawn from the secrets of the numbers and the interlocking of the letters.

And know — may God grant us and you success — that the secrets of God, exalted is He, and the objects of His knowledge — the subtle and the dense, the celestial and the terrestrial, those of the Dominion (malakūt) and those of the Kingdom (mulk) — are according to two relations: numbers and letters. So the secrets of the letters lie in the numbers, and the self-disclosures of the numbers lie in the letters. The celestial numbers belong to the spiritual beings, and the letters to the circles of the corporeal things and of the things of the Dominion. And the numbers are the secret of words, and the letters the secret of acts. So the world of the Throne is numbers, and the world of the Footstool is letters; and the relation of the letters to the numbers is as the relation of the Footstool to the Throne. And by the secret of the numbers absolute power is understood; and that is because /fol. 68v./ the One — glorified and exalted — praised Himself by the secret of the numbers, saying: and We suffice as reckoners (Q 21:47); and He made His praise of the letters revert upon you, in His words, exalted is He: Recite in the name of your Lord— up to His words, exalted is He — who taught by the pen (Q 96:1–4). And the bodies, which are of the relation of the letters, [hold] that which is not known in the world of the numbers. And since the Vast Footstool is joined to the essence of the Throne, and the second Throne is joined to the essence of the encompassing Footstool — so that the parts of the one of them are the first and the last — the configuration of the letters came to be from the numbers. And likewise the last degree of the letters is the first degree of the numbers, and the last degree of the numbers is the first degree of the letters. So by the secret of the numbers is understood the secret of the Lordly intellect, and by the secret of the letters is understood the secret of the spiritual spirit. And the last degree of the intellect is the first degree of the celestial soul, and that is the first effusion — just as the letters (ḥurūf) are taken from ḥarf al-shayʾ, which is its edge; and so the number is its beginning and its middle, and for each thing its beginning is a middle. And by the secret of the letters is understood the secret of the highest Footstool and of the most resplendent Vast Footstool. And that is because the essences among the celestial things — the celestial and the terrestrial — differ by the difference of their own essences, the Footstool being in the highest; and [so too] the difference of their turnings and of their phases within the Vast Footstool, and the configuration of the causes of the spirit, and the leaping of the intellect within a land in the uttermost Footstool. So the Vast Footstool is the first of the principles of the Throne, from the relation of the emanations of the realities of the Kingdom, which are the celestial spheres; and the highest Footstool — this is the first of the emanations within the realities of the Dominion; and the drawing of sustaining supply of the last degree among the terrestrial things is the first degree among the celestial things.

And know that the uttermost Throne is the first effusion, by the first light; and the Vast Footstool is an effusion by the second light; and the highest Footstool is the effusion of the third light. So the first effusion — I mean the third — is the first; and the third is the first of the letters and the last degree of the number; and it is the secret expressed by the reality of mortal humanity (bashariyya), wherein lies the clear proof. He said, exalted is He: Truly I am creating a mortal man from clay (Q 38:71). Then, after that, when the two preceding effusions were completed, his being addressed became necessary; and so the address fell upon him by the name of the human reality (insāniyya), and He said, exalted is He: And when I have shaped him and breathed into him of My spirit (Q 38:72), [and so on to the end of] the verse. And the second effusion is from the parts of the number, and it is the relation of the beginnings of the letters and of their ends. And the third effusion, which is the principles of the numbers, is the meeting-place of the two seas, and it is the outpourer of the two effusions and the secret of the lofty inbreathing. For that reason He said, exalted is He: And when I have shaped him and breathed into him of My spirit, then fall down before him in prostration (Q 38:72) — meaning the two latter effusions and the first effusion. So the world in its entirety, celestial and terrestrial, [subsists] by the reality of these three effusions. /fol. 69r./ And among [the people of] the world there is he who has perfected one effusion of them, and among them he who has perfected two effusions of them, and among them he who has perfected all three — and he is the intelligent one, the all-comprehending Pole (quṭb). And for that reason the bearer is fixed, and [fixed] for their essences, upon the root of the effusion of its known footstools; from the secret of these realities are their numbers, and there is no alteration for the essences of their mass. There appears to him, in the world of the evident reality of mortal humanity — which is the secret of composition, and which is the realities of the highest Footstool — and that is in the world of the Kingdom; and there appears to him, in the world of the human reality, the secret of the Vast Footstool, the world of the Omnipotence (jabarūt), wherein he witnesses the world of the realities of the terrestrial intermediate states (barzakhiyyāt) that are joined between the realities of the two inbreathings; and there appears to him, in the realities of the celestial spirit, the sign of the uttermost Footstool, so that within it are supplied the realities of the arising of the hereafter — that is, the reality of the inbreathing of the resurrection. So his essence is perfected, and his acts become manifest, and his attributes are realized. And whoever departs from the straight line to the deviant line has departed from the absolute and entered into particularization; because the deviant, when it is joined to a deviant and you extend them both, the two meet; whereas the straight, when it is joined to a straight and you extend them both to their equilibrium, the two do not come into equilibrium. And there make the two of them revolve: manifestation, and growth, and the renowned vegetation — the Wise — by the number that comes to an end. So whoever fulfils it, when he passes over to the barzakh world, fulfils the realities of the three [effusions] belonging to the Throne and to the Footstool. And when you have paid it out in full — and the first effusion, which is of the relation of the highest Footstool, not the lowest, belonging to the things of the Dominion — [there comes] a torment of configuring, and burning, and the closing over of layer upon layer, and hand and heel mingled with the sulphur of distance, blazing with the fires of the incendiary letters of the heart, and the loss of hearing, hemming [him] in; and there is completed this pitch-dark, subtle span mingled with wrath. May God, exalted is He, grant us and you refuge from this coal-black abyss (daraka), and from the pitch-dark quaking, and from the life of banishment.

Then he is transferred to the second phase of the torment, which is the torment of the human reality — just as the first torment was [that of] the reality of the bearer of the dense corporeal frame. So he in whom is the second effusion, which is the Vast Footstool, is tormented; that is the torment of the imaging of the reversal and of the stripping away of the true powers of the bodies, by the inverting of the volitions from the primordial nature of the reality to the inward of the tormenting wisdom. And so the essences of the inward forms are cast to him; and whenever anything of them pleases him, his volition strains toward it, that he may be transformed within it essentially, and thereupon the torment fixes itself upon him. And what has come forth to him of the outward of the form is multiplied, until that form exacts from him its reality in full and then separates from him. Thereupon he returns to the tormenting power, and he witnesses another form, and there is multiplied for him, from sense-perception,

within it in redoubled multiples. So his will aspires toward it, and it is turned back upon him, and he finds — from the redoubling of the pains and the torment and the kinds of courses [they run] — what makes him wish he might not see them. And he remains within it as long as /fol. 69v./ God, exalted is He, wills, according to the determination of its density and its subtlety, until he pays in full the whole of that Footstool-form, all of it. And that is [contained] in the secret of His word, exalted is He: Whenever their skins are roasted through — up to — the torment (Q 4:56). And "the skins" refers back to them in accordance with the tormenting power; while the substitution [that befalls] the essences of the forms refers back to the Lordly sending-down, so as to weigh that form down. For it possesses beauty, inasmuch as its placing is in the Footstool; and the numbers of its torment are multiplied only by the multiplication of the modes of its beauty. And the torment returns upon him by the Lordly overturning, while the beauty remains in the tormented essence. God, exalted is He, has said concerning the meaning of that: Then there shall be struck between them a wall having a gate: its inner side, therein is mercy; and its outer side, facing it, is the torment (Q 57:13). And if you wish to witness the reality of absolute, arriving beauty — how it was overturned into the very essence of the ugliness that is cast far off, while it is itself [unchanged] — the overturning is not in its essence, nor in its attributes, nor in its acts; rather it is the mirror of the brought-into-being, which discloses itself within the realities of the Bringer-into-being, glorified and exalted. And the first Bringer-into-being makes beneficence beautiful for whomever He brings into being: [it is] either a world of grace or a world of justice. So the world of grace is the light of the right Handful, and the world of justice is the secret of the left Handful; and thus every mercy from Him is grace, and every retribution from Him is justice.

Let us now return to the verification of that to which we have called attention and to which we have pointed with the subtleties of thought — the line of the breaths, inasmuch as they are qualities and not inasmuch as they are essences — [taken] from the word of the High, the Most High, informing concerning the absolute secret, the manifest Truth, the light that guides to the straight and upright light, the highest secret and the most sublime balance: His mighty Book, and its recitation, the Qurʾān. The sense understood from that is: Say: for those who believe it is guidance and healing; and those who do not believe — in their ears is a deafness, and it is a blindness upon them— in the abode of the barzakh — those are called from a far-off place (Q 41:44). And likewise: "Say: for those who believe" — in the abode of the kingdom (mulk) — "it is guidance"; in the abode of the barzakh, "healing". And likewise: "it is for those who do not believe: in their ears is a deafness, and it is a blindness upon them" — in the abode of the barzakh — "those are called", from the tormented configurative forms, "from a far-off place", because of the deafness of their ears. So when he has paid in full with all the forms, their essences follow one upon another with the variation of their genera and the renewal of their torment; there is stripped from him the speculative, form-giving, imaginative [reading for the edition's] power, and the fixed forms of the torment fade away from him. And this is the torment of the third effusion, the high one, and it is the relation of the uttermost Footstool; and it is the torment of the first rank of the numbers, which adjoins the first of the extremities of the letters; and it is the torment of the spirit, expressed by length and breadth and purification (tazkiya). And this is the most severe of torment: speech is annihilated by reason of the severance, and vision is annihilated by reason of vision, and purification is annihilated by reason of distance. So they are in absolute abysses and burning fires. If they thirst [the edition adds here, unconstruable in the clause] from the intensity of the blaze, they are given to drink of the stripping away of purification. As for the terrestrial letters, they sever /fol. 70r./ their bowels — [that is,] their religious thoughts; and they are fed, if they hunger, from the blindness of the absence of vision and from the Zaqqūm of wrath, which is Majesty; and they are clothed, if they are naked, from the darkness of the desolation of the absence of vision, with garments of pitch — the closing shut of the regions — with thirst, from the wrongdoing amid the befouling. The true relation is by letters that blaze up and numbers that grow heavy, until His high command and His fulfilling decree take shape in the relation of those concerning whom He said: their being safeguarded is annihilated in the three worlds; God will not speak to them in the third world; and for them is a painful torment in the eternal abiding — I mean, the abiding in the graves, in the continuance of their essences amid the kinds of hindrances. Then at that moment the veil is lifted from the eye of the human inner sight, and there appear to him the secrets of the letters of the kingdom (mulk) and the reality of the numbers of the dominion (malakūt): his standing [readingfor the edition's] at the Spring of Life — I mean the honoured Pool (al-ḥawḍ) set apart for the Chosen and Magnified Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace. This is if he draws near in the barzakh world; otherwise the decree pursues him, and the torment cuts him off, and the numbering seizes him, and the enclosure fixes his gaze in a stare, until the Day of the Resurrection of Gathering; and so this standing is paid in full. And if anything remains, then [it is] in the greater Fire, wherein he neither dies nor lives. [So much] for what we wished to make plain and stipulated to explain, for the uttermost effusion has brought us through to a sufficiency in full. And we did not intend to expound the reality of the barzakh in this place, until its proper place should come, if God, exalted is He, wills.

As for what we have mentioned of the secret of the subtle things (laṭāʾif) that subsist through the dense things (kathāʾif) — understand its secret and you will know. And the truth of the Real is the secret of certainty, to which the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — called attention by his saying: ((Whoever knows his own soul knows his Lord; and there is nothing more noble, nor higher, nor greater than your knowing your Lord.)) So whoever grasps this subtlety grasps the secret of the subtle soul and its relation to the dense things. So understand from this secret the preservation of the secret of conjunction, by way of the manner of the knowledge of the soul and the inmost core of the means of the spiritual disciplines (riyāḍāt) that lead to that in its entirety. And after that there will be opened upon you, from the divine effusion and the Lordly fragrance, that which will bring you forth from the circle of compositional confinement into the circle of universal absoluteness; and this covering will be removed, and the space will grow wide for you, and you will ascend to the Lote-Tree of the Boundary (sidrat al-muntahā), and you will walk at proud ease in the midst of the Garden of Refuge (jannat al-maʾwā). I have brought forth this Lordly subtlety and this Sufi glimpse only in quest of the good pleasure of God, offering it as a treasure laid up before my intimate converse [with Him], so that its suns may be beheld by him from whose eye of inner sight the disease of ophthalmia has kept away [readingfor the edition's

,]and in whose world of thought the encrusting sediment has dissolved away. And I hope that he may be my companion in the Highest Assembly and my sitting-companion in the uttermost Meadow, in accordance with what God, exalted is He, has urged in His mighty Book, in His word, exalted is He: And aid one another in righteousness and in God-fearing (Q 5:2). And the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((A man's faith is not complete until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.))

And another subtlety: /fol. 70v./ that the barzakh abode stands in need of the realities of the things of the kingdom (mulkiyyāt), and that it is only through it that the barzakh-realities are reflected back. So tomorrow there will be the moment of [divine] determination, with presence of heart and life of the inmost core — the cleaver of the manifest unseen, and the hidden secret, and the shining light, and pure thought: keep to it! For there is no avoiding what has emerged of the plainness of expression where allusion could not realize it; and this goes back to our own deliverance. And I hold from God the greatest covenant and compact upon whoever is characterized by purity and is mantled in the robe of fidelity: that whenever they peruse the pages of this [book] — the spirits being the place of manifestation of the corporeal frames — they lower their gaze from the indecencies of the wording, and look with the eye of perfection upon whatever is hidden from the grasping of them; and let them pray to God, exalted is He, for me, for whatever has proved sound for them in that upright canon and that straight path. That is called to mind only by his saying — peace be upon him: ((Whoever institutes a good practice has its reward and the reward of whoever acts by it until the Day of Resurrection.)) May God aid you to understand it, and make its knowledge easy for you, and guide you to the keeping of it concealed.

And know that the parts of the world, celestial and terrestrial, are gathered into parts whose number is three thousand thousand thousand, four hundred thousand thousand, and sixteen [3,400,000,016]; for your density pertaining to the kingdom (mulk) is the manifest relation to the eight, and the relation of your awe pertaining to the dominion (malakūt) is to a class of one thousand thousand, and one hundred thousand thousand, and eighteen thousand thousand, and one hundred thousand, and forty thousand, and two hundred and twelve [119,140,212]. And all these numbers you have contained within your dense essence and within your subtle awe, by power. So, as to what has preceded: this is the delimitation of the subtle and the dense things within the composite constitution and the divine attribute. Whoever lights upon this reality attains to the secret of thankfulness; and whoever attains to the secret of thankfulness has attained to the valley of the first principles of love. We do not wish to expound that, because of its evidentness, and lest the discourse be drawn out away from the purpose bound up with it. So when you desire the spirits for what has been mentioned above: that which stands [as their sustainer], of the divine, celestial Spirit — the great, the beloved, the intended, the manifest, the luminous, the master — is one part out of thirty thousand thousand thousand [30,000,000,000]. And this is the part complete in the dense things of the composite world. So if you wish to understand that, divide the total number — which is thirty-two thousand thousand thousand, six hundred thousand thousand, and fifty-eight thousand [32,600,058,000] — by two hundred thousand and sixty-five [200,065]; and whatever comes out, add it together as a number: that is the resultant, the root.
